newsitem.title: USA: Bombs rock abortion clinic in Tulsa, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Bombs rock abortion clinic in Tulsa, no injuries.

text.p: Two bomb explosions rocked an abortion clinic in Tulsa on Sunday, just three days after six people were injured in a similar attack on an Atlanta clinic.

Police Sgt. Wayne Allen said the two bombs exploded seconds apart just outside the Reproductive Services of Tulsa clinic shortly after 3 p.m. (2100 GMT), but no one was injured because it was closed for the day.
"Fortunately, there was no one inside at the time," he said. "There was moderate damage at the rear of the building. The explosion penetrated the building and destroyed a few glass panels inside."

Bomb experts from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms were deployed to check the building for clues. They moved cautiously at first because of fears of a booby trap, but sniffer dogs found no other explosive devices.
On Thursday two bombs ripped through an abortion clinic in Atlanta. The second blast came about one hour after the first and injured six people.
Sunday's bombings marked the second time the one-story Tulsa clinic, which is located in a middle-class residential and business neigborhood, has been attacked so far this year.
On New Year's Day, assailants lobbed two Molotov cocktails at the building and caused some damage but no injuries.
The clinic employs about 15 people and offers family planning and adoption services as well as abortions.
Allen said the FBI was looking for possible links to the previous attacks but that no arrests had yet been made.
"We have no suspects in mind or any information that it is linked to the Jan. 1 incident or the Atlanta bombing," he said.
